public_profile_enrichment.method: Public-source research (IRS Form 990 via ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer, wemeasure.org, Candid, news) synthesized 2026-07-10. Every fact below carries its source and a confidence level. The 'Only You Can Supply This' list holds items genuinely not public that only Measure can provide. This block corrects and extends the base profile (for example, leadership is 'President & Founder,' not CEO/ED). A second exhaustive eight-lane public-source sweep (2026-07-10) added leadership demographics, the founder's profile, program metrics, publications, partners, and 990 financial detail: see the leadership demographics section, the 'Not Knowable From Any Source' and 'Findable, but Behind a Paywall or a Login' lists, and 'Where the Record Disagrees With Itself' for that detail.
public_profile_enrichment.operating_budget_band: Approximately $1.0M-$1.25M per year, best proxied by FY2024 (fiscal year ending December 2024) total expenses of $1,220,876 per ProPublica/IRS Form 990. On a broader recent-years view the band is roughly $700K-$1.3M and trending upward. This sits comfortably inside the $500K-$10M range: every fiscal year from FY2020 onward has total expenses above $500K, and FY2022-FY2024 revenue all exceeds $700K, well below the $10M ceiling. (Caveat: if a funder measures strictly by revenue, FY2021 revenue was $325K, below $500K, but expenses that year were $563K, and FY2022-FY2024 clear $500K on both measures.)
public_profile_enrichment.financial_summary: ProPublica (mirroring IRS Form 990 data) holds filings from FY ending Nov 2018 through FY ending Dec 2024. The org shows steep, sustained growth: it graduated from 990-EZ (~$46K revenue in FY Nov 2018; ~$188K in FY Nov 2019) to a full Form 990 starting FY Dec 2019, when it changed its fiscal-year-end from November to December. Revenue climbed from $568,750 (FY2020) with a one-year dip to $325,374 (FY2021, the only net-loss year, expenses $563,571), then $745,052 (FY2022), $1,254,853 (FY2023), and $1,268,433 (FY2024). Expenses tracked upward: $409,830 (2020) → $703,389 (2022) → $1,009,252 (2023) → $1,220,876 (2024), with the org running an operating surplus in FY2022-FY2024. Net assets grew steadily to $497,818 at year-end 2024. The most recent return is the full Form 990 for FY ending December 2024, filed October 1, 2025; the calendar-year FY2025 return is not yet public and would not typically be filed until late 2026.

verified_facts.value: The CARE Model is delivered to grassroots orgs as the 'Free Data Support Grant': each selected org receives a $25,000 in-kind grant plus a $1,000 participant stipend (two $500 direct deposits, Mar 15 & Jun 15). Eligibility gate: annual operating budget under $500,000; community-led governance; serves historically marginalized communities; 501(c)(3)/charter school/community college/university/faith-based/grassroots status; active Measure Ignite account. 2026 cycle ran Oct 7-Nov 21, 2025 (notifications Jan 9, 2026); one application per org per year; reopens 2027.
verified_facts.note: New, materially extends the profile: concrete per-org value ($25K in-kind + $1K stipend) and the under-$500K budget eligibility gate. Annual awardee/cohort count not published.

verified_facts.value: CARE Model v4.0 (Community, Advocacy, Resilience, Evidence): 12 facilitated meetings over 3-6 months across three phases (identify systemic barriers → define community-led solutions → build a Community Mobilization Guide), with deliverables like stakeholder maps and historic timelines. Offered as a product family: core Free Data Support Grant; CARE Model Facilitator Training (yields 'certified facilitator'); CARE Model for Disruptive Changemakers; and CARE Model for AI Systems.
verified_facts.note: New duration/deliverables and the multi-track structure. No cohort size/cost/duration published for the sub-tracks.

verified_facts.value: '25+ grassroots organizations supported across Texas' via the CARE Model / Free Data Support program, with institutional partnerships naming the City of Austin, The Thinkery, and Huston-Tillotson University.
verified_facts.note: New program-specific count (distinct from top-line '84+/93+/104+ orgs with a Measure tool'). The Thinkery is a new named partner.

verified_facts.value: Communities in the Loop is Measure's flagship civic-tech/AI-governance initiative, using the CARE Model to convene residents, educators, technologists, and youth to define responsible/ethical AI. Named partners: the Austin AI Alliance and the City of Austin. Delivered as six Austin community sessions (themes: Responsible & Ethical AI; Public Trust & Accountability; Health & AI; Digital Equity; Civic Participation). Residents named six priorities: transparency, accountability, human oversight, privacy, AI literacy, and environmental justice.
verified_facts.note: New named partners (Austin AI Alliance, City of Austin), session themes, and community-named priorities.

verified_facts.value: 'Nearly 400 residents engaged' across Communities in the Loop convenings; six community sessions planned across Austin by 2026.
verified_facts.note: New hard reach number (~400 residents), previously a profile gap. Downstream AI policies actually changed remain unquantified.

verified_facts.value: Financially Lit & Funding Ready: a six-week virtual series (Tuesdays, e.g. Sept 15-Oct 20, 2026, 12-1 PM CT) for nonprofit/grassroots leaders, each session with up to three expert panelists (topics span scarcity-to-sustainability fundraising, nonprofit financial structures/tax compliance, budgeting, reserves/banking, Black philanthropy, and data storytelling via Measure Ignite). 2025 outcomes: 386 registrants, 200 live participants (5 sessions), 9.3/10 satisfaction, 94% gained new donor-engagement strategies. Stated program cost $36,000. 2026 goals include 300 live participants, expansion to 5 new regions, and 30 orgs receiving 1:1 technical assistance.
verified_facts.note: New full curriculum, quantitative outcomes, and a published $36K program budget resolve the profile's cohort-counts gap.

verified_facts.value: Measure Ignite ('the community power-building database') is an equity-centered platform built with Black/Brown/Indigenous orgs, addressing three gaps (no data-management tech, limited networking, low visibility) via four features: Manage Metrics, Report Impact, Get Matched, and Find Funding. ~300 users; ~5 years building (idea 2021 → 2024 beta → 2025 Ignite 2.0). Its conceptual precursor was 'Measure Connect,' Styles' SSRC Just Tech Fellowship project. Development partners: MIT Solve, SSRC, and Philanthropitch; foundation partner The Black Fund.
verified_facts.note: New four features + the 'Measure Connect → Ignite' lineage (SSRC source). Philanthropitch is a new partner. An active Ignite account is a prerequisite for the Free Data Support Grant.

verified_facts.value: The Innocence Initiative educates on adultification bias against Black and Brown children via data storytelling centering Black girls, trainings for parents/teachers/legal professionals, advocacy, a 'Girl Squad'/'Travis County Girl Squad' mentorship program (ages 13-17), and a partnership with Truckers Against Trafficking on the 'Protecting Our Daughters' campaign. It is a 5-org coalition (with Girl Scouts of Central Texas, Lone Star Justice Alliance, Hearts 2 Heal, Community Advocacy and Healing Project) aiming to protect 35,000+ girls of color; Georgetown supplied the original adultification research.
verified_facts.note: New: Truckers Against Trafficking partnership, Girl Squad mentorship, and the 35,000+ scope. Extends the profile's coalition fact.

verified_facts.value: Reach: 'Over 1,000 attorneys' trained (program page); a virtual racial-equity training drew 200 registered attorneys with 700+ seeking Texas State Bar CLE credit (Sept 2020); 5 community-led sessions reached 535 parents/teachers/advocates; the 'Hey Sis! Be You!' comic (story of Grace, who becomes the first Black female president) was distributed to 15,000 households; 10+ trainings; work helped inform Travis County's COVID-era youth release. Published resources include an 11-page School & Local Policy Brief (Dec 2020) with 10 policy recommendations.
verified_facts.note: New granular metrics (700+ attorneys sought CLE, 535 reached, 15,000 households refines profile's '15,000 comic books'). Youth-release influence is medium (attributional).

verified_facts.value: Measure supported CROWN Act passage in Austin and Pflugerville, contributing to the statewide Texas CROWN Act (led by State Rep. Rhetta A. Bowers). The impact page also lists an 'OCR' (Office for Civil Rights) policy win alongside the CROWN Act.
verified_facts.note: Extends profile (Austin 2022 + Texas 2023): Pflugerville and the OCR win are new; the OCR specifics are unconfirmed.

verified_facts.value: Community Data Gatherings are community-centered, non-extractive sessions built around a partner nonprofit's mission, in four steps: (1) Sacred, Accessible Spaces (trusted venues); (2) Community Care (food); (3) AI Literacy (Measure LIT); (4) CARE Model breakouts. Each produces a 'community-informed case study' the partner owns. Measure has held these at Huston-Tillotson's Dickey-Lawless Auditorium. No participation counts published.
verified_facts.note: New four-step format; embeds Measure LIT AI literacy into every gathering.

verified_facts.value: Direct Evaluation Services ('Hire Our Team') is Measure's fee-for-service, mixed-methods program-evaluation line for nonprofits and public agencies, a distinct earned-revenue offering separate from its free/grant programs. This aligns with the 990 data showing program-service (earned) revenue reaching 31% of FY2024 revenue.
verified_facts.note: New named earned-revenue program. No client counts published on the page.

verified_facts.value: Measure publishes its own AI governance: a 'Measure AI Acceptable Use Policy V1' (March 2026) aligned to Texas's TRAIGA and NIST AI RMF 1.0, with the principle that 'Communities review every public-facing AI output.' One active tool is named ('Engagement Finder,' using Google Gemini) with defined permitted/prohibited uses and a 24-hour-to-1-week incident-response protocol.
verified_facts.note: New governance content useful for AI-funder capacity/credibility narratives.

verified_facts.value: Measure structures its work around '14 ethical commitments' organized under three pillars: 'Voice first,' 'Equity Centered always,' and 'Do no harm.'
verified_facts.note: New proposal-ready methodology/values framing device.

verified_facts.value: The Community-Engaged Research Course (CERC) is now presented as the 'Grassroots Research Studio @ Huston-Tillotson University.' Reported metrics unchanged: 69+ students trained, 23 nonprofits supported, 88.4% underrepresented students; 2019 inaugural HTU cohort, 2021 Texas State University expansion; timeline 2019-2025.
verified_facts.note: New branding for the CERC program the profile already tracks.

verified_facts.value: Top-line JavaScript counters have climbed well past the profile's stale snapshot ($783,893 / 82+): 'CARE Model grants distributed' now renders between ~$794,557 and ~$985,888; 'Orgs supported with a Measure tool' between 84+ and 104+; '% nonprofits reporting improved storytelling & measurement' 65-80%; plus '51% increase in fundraising confidence' and '32 new Measure evaluators trained.'
verified_facts.note: Updates the profile's stale figures but confirms its caution: these are volatile animated counters that render inconsistently across pages same-day. Cite the label, not the exact digits.

verified_facts.value: Free Data Support (redistributing data power to Black/Brown/Indigenous-led orgs, 2020-present): $950K+ in-kind value delivered, 63+ organizations served, 3,000+ hours donated; About-page 'decade overview' adds '15,000 households reached' and '88.4% underrepresented researchers.'
verified_facts.note: Confirms profile's $950K/63+/3,000-hours; adds the 15,000-households metric. Note MIT Solve dates the 3,000+ hours 'since 2019' while the impact page says 2020-21.

verified_facts.value: Need-framing statistics Measure cites: '79% of Black-led organizations lack systems for collecting data' (Measure 2021 research, rationale for Ignite) and '1% — the combined philanthropic funding to Black communities' (attributed to the National Center for Responsive Philanthropy).
verified_facts.note: New citable Statement-of-Need anchors. The 1% figure is a third-party (NCRP) statistic, not a Measure outcome.

verified_facts.value: Measure maintains a large public 'Data Gallery' of roughly 61 works (2020-2026) in recurring formats: Black Papers (flagship, branded '[Title]: A Lived-Experience Black Paper'), Field Studies, Policy Briefs, Historical Timelines, and Press, far more than the 3 publications in the profile.
verified_facts.note: The ~61-item library's EXISTENCE is high-confidence, but ~30 entries stamped 'December 2020' are likely a bulk-upload artifact, and a few (Georgetown 'Girlhood Interrupted,' Annie E. Casey 'Kids Count,' TNTP 'Opportunity Myth') are curated external references, not Measure-authored. Treat pre-2024 dates/authorship as medium/low confidence.

verified_facts.value: 'The State of Black Lives in Austin: A Lived-Experience Black Paper', 64 pages (~29.9 MB), released March 11, 2024 with the Austin Justice Coalition; authors T. Harrison (Tiffanie Harrison), M. Styles, and P. Blanc. It compares the City's 2008 African American Quality of Life Report (which outlined 56 initiatives, mostly never sustained) against a 2023 assessment across six domains, deliberately posing accountability questions rather than new recommendations and calling for an impartial audit. Landing page wemeasure.org/the-state-of-black-austin is now live (previously 404'd).
verified_facts.note: Extends profile: three named authors, page/file size, the 2008 baseline (56 initiatives), and the 'questions not recommendations' framing.

verified_facts.value: Additional findings beyond the profile's headline set. Arts & Culture: Black communities received only ~2% of City cultural funding (2015-2021) and 90%+ (reported 93%) of surveyed Black musicians report booking discrimination. Health: African Americans had the highest mortality in 4 of 7 leading causes of death in Travis County and the lowest life expectancy. Neighborhood Sustainability: Black population share stagnated ~7.25-8.52% (2016-2021) amid disproportionate displacement.
verified_facts.note: Multi-source corroborated (CultureMap, KUT, Austin Monitor). Strong equity anchors.

verified_facts.value: 'Drivers Contributing to the Decline of the Black Population in Austin' (Black Paper, June 2022), a community-led survey (very likely the same work as the '212 Catalysts & AALI Black Austin Survey Report,' authored by Tiffanie Harrison, May 2022, with 212 Catalysts and the African American Leadership Institute). Findings: 88% cited unaffordable cost of living as a reason to leave; 80% reported a lack of belonging; 47% had experienced racism in Austin; three primary barriers were policy, affordability, and sense of belonging.
verified_facts.note: New publication. Sample size disputed (see conflicts: 336 vs 375). 'Same document as the AALI survey' is a strong inference, not confirmed.

verified_facts.value: 'Interrogating Public Safety Metrics: A Lived-Experience Black Paper', 27 pages, August 2024 (gallery lists Sept 2024); authors P. Blanc, M. Styles & J. Aghimien, in partnership with the Initiative for Law, Societies, and Justice at the University of Texas at Austin. Reframes public safety from enforcement to 'physical, psychological, and economic security' and introduces Measure Ignite as a platform for community-driven safety metrics.
verified_facts.note: Extends profile's bare title with page count, authors, and the UT Austin academic partner.

verified_facts.value: 'Breaking Barriers: Bridging the Nonprofit Board Representation Gap: A Lived-Experience Black Paper', 17 pages (~7.1 MB), August 2023 (gallery lists April 2024); authors T. N. Ricks & H. Chun, in partnership with The New Philanthropists.
verified_facts.note: Extends profile's bare title with page count, date, authors, and partner.

verified_facts.value: AI-governance publication cluster (most citable for AI-funder proposals): (1) 'Community in the Loop: Municipal AI Governance in Austin' (Black Paper, 2026), reports 400+ residents shaped a framework for AI transparency and human oversight; (2) 'Community in the Loop: Engaging Austin Residents on AI Accountability' (Field Study, March 2026, 9 pages; authors Styles, Williams, Wallace, Merida; partners City of Austin and the Austin AI Alliance); (3) 'Interrogative Reasoning and "Human in the Loop"' (Just Tech/SSRC essay, June 2026).
verified_facts.note: New. Field-study metadata fetch-confirmed; the Municipal AI Governance '400+ residents' figure is from the gallery listing only.

verified_facts.value: Recent/other Measure-authored works: 'Hotel Occupancy Tax' (Black Paper, Feb 2025); 'Highlighting Lived Experiences of Pre-Diabetes & Type 2 Diabetes' (Field Study, Dec 2025); a 2020-2021 policing series (e.g., 'Dollars & Sense,' 'The Costs of Police Violence: Measuring Misconduct,' 'Public Safety Vision 2020'); a Black-girls/adultification series (e.g., 'Disrupting the Jezebel Stereotype,' Jan 2023; 'Women of Color Should Have a Voice…,' Nov 2022); and equity Black Papers ('Centering the Experience of Black-Led Nonprofits in Austin,' June 2021; 'Hire + Retain Black Teachers,' May 2022; 'Addressing the Digital Divide in Austin: Residential Technology Study,' Oct 2022).
verified_facts.note: Titles/dates from the gallery listing; internal findings not fetched. The Residential Technology Study is the published companion to the City of Austin digital-inclusion work already in the profile.

verified_facts.value: The Black Fund (of Central Texas): founder Meme Styles is a co-founder (with Dr. Colette Pierce Burnette, then Huston-Tillotson president, and Kendra Garrett). Founded 2020, formalized 2022; has distributed ~$1.2M to 72 Black-led Central Texas organizations. Austin Community Foundation served as its founding fiscal-sponsor/incubator before it spun out.
verified_facts.note: Deepens the profile (which lists The Black Fund only as an Ignite foundation partner): Measure's founder co-created it. Also adds a third distinct ACF touchpoint (incubation) beyond the $6K grant and the Google.org fund.

verified_facts.value: HBCU AI Conference & Training Summit, hosted at Huston-Tillotson University and co-chaired by Meme Styles with Chris Hyams (former CEO of Indeed; HTU trustee). 2nd annual held March 10-11, 2026 in Austin, drawing 25+ HBCUs (600+ participants expected). Styles and Hyams also co-authored a March 11, 2026 Fortune op-ed on HBCUs leading AI.
verified_facts.note: New flagship annual convening deepening the HTU relationship, plus a named individual/corporate connection (Chris Hyams / former Indeed CEO). No evidence of a direct Indeed corporate grant to Measure.

verified_facts.value: City of Austin (FY2024): per Measure's own IRS Schedule O narrative, it 'provided strategic program support for two projects with the City of Austin (specifically the HOT Program and Watershed Department).' A distinct, more recent government engagement than the 2021 Residential Technology Study already in the profile.
verified_facts.note: New, and corroborated in the org's own 990 words. 'HOT Program' most likely Hotel Occupancy Tax (cultural funding) vs. Homeless Outreach Team, unresolved. Contract dollar values not published.

verified_facts.value: Per the FY2024 Schedule O narrative, Measure 'provided direct services to four major partner organizations through data and evaluation support aligned with our Innocence Initiative' and delivered four adultification-bias trainings and a virtual leadership summit. The four organizations are not named publicly.
verified_facts.note: Confirms a fee/service client model; the four names are a still_findable gap.

verified_facts.value: Measure's original flagship program (absent from the current site) was the Big Data & Community Policing (BDCP) Conference & Forums, a multi-day Austin event convening police, community, activists, academics, and developers around open data and evidence-based policing. Mayor Steve Adler called it 'Austin's #1 Technology Project.' Named partners/sponsors: Mark43 (policing software; CEO Scott Crouch), the Austin Police Department, Huston-Tillotson University, Capital Metro, and the American Society of Evidence Based Policing.
verified_facts.note: Net-new founding-era signature initiative establishing deep early ties (APD, HTU predating CERC, Capital Metro, Mark43) and a citable Mayor Adler endorsement.

verified_facts.value: Measure's original community-policing measurement methodology (precursor to the CARE Model) was built by adapting Stacey Barr's PuMP performance-measurement program and U.S. military strategic-planning frameworks. The CARE Model itself was co-designed through facilitated dialogue with ~400 community members and 25 community leaders, community-built, not authored top-down.
verified_facts.note: Net-new intellectual lineage (consistent with the founder's GWU performance-measurement cert and Army background); the ~400/25 co-design scale is single-source (VoyageDallas), treat as approximate.

verified_facts.value: Styles built Measure as a side venture while employed full-time by the State of Texas, working her 9-to-5, then building Measure roughly 10 p.m.-2 a.m., starting with a team of four Austin community leaders (activism, technology, research, education). The APD origin quote is sharper than the current site: on a community-policing panel she asked 'Where is the damn data?' and the panel could not answer.
verified_facts.note: Net-new founding-grit color extending the profile's 'team of four.' The 'Where is the damn data?' quote came via a soulciti search snippet (host timed out), confirm against primary.

verified_facts.value: Measure conducted its own data analysis of the Dallas juvenile curfew ordinance, using data to argue the law was not evidence-based; Dallas police leadership nonetheless retained it. Styles cites this as a case of evidence meeting institutional resistance.
verified_facts.note: Fills the profile's explicit 'no Dallas-specific programming/clients' gap. Single-source interview; specific deliverable not located.

verified_facts.value: Below-topline revenue mix (ProPublica/990): FY2024 total $1,268,433 = contributions $873,759 (68.9%) + program-service (earned) revenue $393,024 (31.0%). Earned revenue up +196.8% YoY. FY2023 = contributions $1,127,396 (89.8%) + program-service $132,419, with a net fundraising loss of -$4,965. Prior years: FY2022 27.4% earned; FY2021 33.1% earned; FY2020 100% contributions; FY2019 majority earned (52.6%). Arc: began earned-heavy (2019) → 100% grant in the 2020 COVID surge → rebuilt to ~31% earned by 2024.
verified_facts.note: New composition detail (profile had only toplines). The 31% earned-revenue share is a fundability strength; corroborated by CauseIQ.

verified_facts.value: FY2024 Schedule B top contributions received: Fidelity Investments Charitable Gift Fund $202,300; Michael & Susan Dell Foundation $169,000; St. David's Foundation $162,000, together = $533,300 (61% of FY2024 contributions). CauseIQ indicates 10 named grants total ('and 7 more,' gated).
verified_facts.note: Updates the profile: Dell rose to $169,000 in FY2024 (the profile's $131,000 is an earlier-year grant, different years, not a contradiction). Top-3 = 61% concentration is a fundability risk worth flagging.

verified_facts.value: Styles is the only compensated officer/board member (all others $0). Her comp: FY2024 $123,075; FY2023 $141,151 (peak); FY2022 $86,826; FY2021 $100,141; FY2020 $91,000 ($84,000 on the amended return); FY2019 $66,576. Non-officer salaries grew from $59,669 (FY2019) → $290,837 (FY2023) → $402,141 (FY2024). FY2024 total W-2 payroll ≈ $525,217 (~43% of $1,220,876 expenses). Six W-2 employees reported on the FY2024 990.
verified_facts.note: New compensation/payroll/headcount detail. The 6 W-2 employees vs ~9 named on the site reconciles as ~3 contractors/fellows. FY2024 payroll count via CauseIQ.

verified_facts.value: FY2024 program-vs-overhead split is only partially public and the two available figures conflict: a computed ratio shows ~76% to programs (≈$928K of $1,220,876), while a ProPublica-derived snippet cites ~$680K (≈56%) tied to a single narrated program line (Part III 4a). The exact Part IX B/C/D column totals are not extractable from free-tier sources.
verified_facts.note: Do not assert 76% as fact in a draft; a funder pulling the 990 could see a lower Part IX ratio. Exact split is in the 990 XML, blocked here, but may still be findable with more effort.

verified_facts.value: Total expenses scaled ~29x in six years: $41,888 (FY2018) → $409,830 (FY2020) → $703,389 (FY2022) → $1,009,252 (FY2023) → $1,220,876 (FY2024). Operating surplus every year except FY2021 (-$238,197, the only deficit). Net assets climbed to $497,818 (FY2024) against total liabilities of only $45,570, a low-debt, positive-net-asset balance sheet.
verified_facts.note: Strengthens the profile's topline series with surplus/deficit and balance-sheet health for an 'organizational financial capacity' section.

verified_facts.value: Measure's Form 990 filings (FY2018-FY2024) include Schedules A, B, C, and O but no Schedule I, and report no cash grants to other organizations. Its self-reported 'CARE Model grants distributed / 82+ orgs supported' therefore reflects in-kind data support, not reportable cash regranting, and cannot be corroborated by a named IRS grantee roster.
verified_facts.note: Important interpretive fact: the 'grants distributed' counter is in-kind value, consistent with the $25K in-kind Free Data Support Grant structure.

Positioning drift, not a factual conflict.
$110,000 single Social Innovation Grant (2019) vs Candid's '~$200,000 collectively invested over time'. Different scopes: single grant vs cumulative.

public_profile_enrichment.is_black_bipoc_led: Measure is Black-woman-led and BIPOC-led/centered, and women-led. The strongest primary source is founder & President Jameila 'Meme' Styles' own first-person statement in a St. David's Foundation-published piece: 'the depth of who we are as Black women data activists' (she/her, per the St. David's Foundation). Its mission redistributes data power to 'Black, Brown, and Indigenous-led organizations,' and its founder is described as 'disrupting traditional research frameworks with BIPOC-led, lived-experience protocols' (per the SSRC Just Tech Fellowship network page). Independent press lists Measure among 'Austin Advocacy Organizations Led by Black Women' (Austin Woman), and Measure/press repeatedly use 'all-Black woman-led nonprofit.' Honesty caveat for grant DEI fields: Measure's own site (wemeasure.org/about) carries no formal 'Black-led/women-led/BIPOC-led' badge; it lists leadership names/photos and BIPOC-centered mission language. Cite the founder's first-person self-identification and independent press, not a website self-label. For a self-reported directory value, confirm the Candid demographic profile (EIN 82-2372196), which was gated (HTTP 402/403) this pass.
